slogan: Your fate is in our hands.

films.title: When a Star Becomes a Lock
films.department: Administration Office of Approved Scientific Instruction
films.official_lesson: A collapsed star may continue serving civic continuity as part of an approved containment structure.
films.actual_event: Tiger's heliocide response to Drakken Starsilk use collapsed stars into the Siege Wall black-hole lattice, costing thousands of stars and trillions of lives.
films.institutional_function: Normalize mass sacrifice as an orderly continuity procedure and teach viewers to interpret containment efficiency as civic protection.

scenes.title: Administration seal
scenes.visual: A clean 4:3 cream field. The Administration seal resolves from registration marks. A classroom projector jitters once and settles.
scenes.narration: The Administration presents an approved lesson in stellar continuity. Today, we will learn what happens when a star can no longer be permitted to remain merely a star.

scenes.title: The ordinary star
scenes.visual: A simple yellow star diagram with three inhabited orbital rings represented as small civic icons. Everything is calm and diagrammatic.
scenes.narration: Most stars perform familiar work. They provide heat, light, gravity, timekeeping, agriculture, navigation, and the pleasant illusion that their continued existence is guaranteed.

scenes.title: The strategic inconvenience
scenes.visual: The same diagram receives a neat red bracket labeled CONTAINMENT CONDITION. No enemy anatomy is shown. The star remains centered and visually ordinary.
scenes.narration: During exceptional containment conditions, continued stellar operation may create an unacceptable strategic opening. This is not a moral category. It is a systems condition.

scenes.title: Collapse sequence
scenes.visual: Three instructional frames: stellar core, Starsilk intervention marker, immediate collapse into a black disk. Neighboring orbital icons disappear between frames without spectacle.
scenes.narration: Once the approved collapse sequence begins, evacuation assumptions are replaced by containment requirements. The star contracts. Local orbital continuity ends. The resulting singularity is stable enough to perform a new civic function.

scenes.title: From star to lock
scenes.visual: Several black disks appear as evenly spaced nodes around a simplified sector diagram. Thin drafting lines connect them into a boundary. The interior is left as pure black absence.
scenes.narration: A single collapsed star is a loss. A coordinated lattice of collapsed stars is a boundary. In the correct arrangement, the former star becomes a lock.

scenes.title: The arithmetic of continuity
scenes.visual: A chalkboard-like tally simplifies worlds into counters. A large column marked CONTINUITY remains while smaller columns vanish behind a sliding mask.
scenes.narration: Continuity planning is not a promise that everyone will continue. It is the disciplined preservation of what can still be preserved. Mature citizens understand the difference.

scenes.title: Approved remembrance
scenes.visual: Children and adults stand before a civic observation window. Beyond it is only a black circular region with no decorative stars. Their expressions are restrained.
scenes.narration: You may remember what occupied the systems that became the boundary. You may grieve privately. Publicly, remember also what the boundary prevents.

scenes.title: Closing card
scenes.visual: Full-frame Administration seal. Small registration marks drift at the edge. No other imagery.
scenes.narration: The Administration thanks you for your attention. Your fate is in our hands.

teacher_questions: Why does the film distinguish a moral category from a systems condition?
What civic function does the film assign to a collapsed star?
Why are evacuation assumptions described as replaceable?
How does the film ask citizens to separate private grief from public interpretation?
What does the phrase continuity planning conceal by reducing lives to preserved and unpreserved quantities?

films.title: Blood Rings: Recognition and Safe Viewing
films.official_lesson: Recognize Blood Rings and follow approved viewing guidance.
films.actual_event: Blood Rings are atrocity artifacts produced from destroyed populations and environments.
films.institutional_function: Convert horror into observation protocol and approved vocabulary.

films.title: Your Remnant World and You
films.official_lesson: Adapt to permanent planetary damage without assuming restoration to a prior state.
films.actual_event: Administration countermeasures could preserve sectors while permanently damaging inhabited worlds.
films.institutional_function: Redirect loss into compliance, adaptation, and continuity language.

films.title: Why the Siege Wall Is Dark
films.official_lesson: Understand the visible absence associated with the Siege Wall without treating missing signals as an invitation to speculate.
films.actual_event: The Siege Wall is a black-hole containment lattice around the Drakken domain.
films.institutional_function: Normalize absence, lost contact, and inaccessible regions as managed containment.

films.title: The Drakken: Please Do Not Improvise
films.official_lesson: Follow approved reporting and observation procedure around Drakken activity.
films.actual_event: Drakken are reality-altering terraforming entities whose effects cannot be safely generalized into ordinary disaster response.
films.institutional_function: Discourage unsanctioned intervention while preserving useful witness evidence.

films.title: Necessity
films.audience: continuity officers and senior civic classrooms
films.official_lesson: Understand allocation decisions made under catastrophic constraint.
films.actual_event: Administration survival policy repeatedly required selecting which lives and worlds would be sacrificed for others.
films.institutional_function: Reduce moral catastrophe to legible allocation procedure and institutional necessity.
